sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Work and Pensions Secretary Pat McFadden confirmed that a staggered age of consent will be discussed. The proposal follows the conviction of comedian Russell Brand, who was jailed for 10-and-a-half years for rape and sexual assault. Campaigner Mia Latter, who alleged abuse by Brand when she was 16, wants relationships between adults and 16 to 17-year-olds criminalised while permitting teenage relationships.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Under UK law, adults of any age can legally have sex with 16 and 17-year-olds. Campaign group Close the Consent Gap argues this creates a power imbalance, as people of this age are classified as children in other legal frameworks. Shadow Work and Pensions Secretary Helen Whately supported having a debate on changing the law.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Pat McFadden said he could not predict the conclusion of age of consent discussions. Meanwhile, Metropolitan Police are investigating comedian David Walliams over alleged serious sexual offences following reports by ITV News and the Guardian, which Walliams strongly denies.

sections.text: Ireland recovered from a sluggish first-half performance to defeat Fiji with a bonus-point win. gist: Greenpeace placed fifteen tonnes of boulders on the seabed in the North Sea.
The boulder barrier overlaps with a planned multi billion pound offshore windfarm site.
Developers are investigating the placement while Greenpeace dismisses any major construction obstacles.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Greenpeace activists dropped numerous heavy stone blocks onto the sea floor off the Norfolk coast to stop bottom trawling. Most of these boulders landed on the planned location for a major offshore windfarm.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The underwater barrier creates an unexpected complication for renewable energy developers planning to construct large windfarms in the area. Developers must now verify boulder locations and investigate potential impacts on upcoming construction.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The energy developer is discussing boulder locations with Greenpeace to update previous seabed surveys. The boulders will likely be removed within months ahead of construction starting next year.

gist: The Guardian is following eight young people searching for work.
Almost a million young people are not in education, employment or training.
Alan Milburn is expected to publish a landmark review on Tuesday.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Guardian launched a series following eight young people aged 20 to 26 searching for work amidst uncertain economic conditions, the aftermath of the Covid pandemic, and the rise of AI. This comes as the number of young people not in education, employment or training reaches a ten-year high.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Being out of work during early adulthood causes profound financial and mental health impacts, including a lifetime earnings loss of up to 300000 pounds for those who reach 24 without working. The youth jobs crisis costs Britain 125 billion pounds a year.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Alan Milburn will publish his final official report and recommendations on Tuesday, warning of structural failure and calling on ministers to reform the benefits system, employment, education, and health policies.
